chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from al-Fudayl, who said:
Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام was asked about a junub who performs ghusl, and some splashes from the ground fall into the vessel.
So he said: “There is no harm in it; this is among that which Allah, the Exalted, has said:”
“He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship.”

key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the ground from which the splash rises
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.حَرَجٍ: undue hardship or constriction in religious practice
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal problem

ai.seo_question: Does splash from the ground entering a water vessel during ghusl affect ritual purity?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that if a person in janabah performs ghusl and some splash from the ground gets into the vessel, there is no problem in that. The Imam عليه السلام supports the ruling by citing the Qur'anic principle that Allah has not placed hardship in the religion, showing ease in matters of ritual purity.
